# Exploration: optional encodings to reduce ash token usage

## Context

Tokens are the operational cost we care about most in this repo. The
ledger already records `tokens_in` / `tokens_out` per call via cl100k_base,
and the established pattern for token reduction is "selective
don't-render in pretty form, full data on the wire" — already present in
`find --with_meta=false`, `grep --files_only`, `grep --no_text`,
`git diff --stat`, `diff --stat`, `git log` body-omission.

The user wants to explore which *encoding-shaped* changes (input and
output) could push token usage further down, without committing to a
specific implementation up front. The plan below is **measurement-first**:
quantify where tokens actually go today before choosing options to ship.

## How tokenization works today (load-bearing facts)

- `tokens_in` is `cl100k_base.Count(proto.PrettyRequest(req))` —
  rebuilt as `ash <verb> --<key1> <val1> --<key2> <val2>` with **keys
  sorted alphabetically**, values via `fmt.Sprintf("%v", v)`. Built from
  the *parsed* args map ([internal/proto/pretty.go:14-30](internal/proto/pretty.go#L14-L30)),
  not the original argv.
- `tokens_out` is `cl100k_base.Count(verbPretty(req, rsp))` — the
  per-verb pretty renderer registered in
  [internal/verbs/verbs.go:46-61](internal/verbs/verbs.go#L46-L61).
  Both counts happen daemon-side at
  [cmd/ashd/main.go:140-142](cmd/ashd/main.go#L140-L142).
- The msgpack wire format is invisible to tokenization. JSON / msgpack
  output modes only matter if an agent opts in.
- `--format` is stripped client-side at
  [cmd/ash/main.go:172-187](cmd/ash/main.go#L172-L187) and never reaches
  the daemon. Adding format awareness to renderers requires plumbing it
  into the request (or extending the per-verb PrettyResponse signature).
- Positional args are explicitly rejected at
  [cmd/ash/main.go:197](cmd/ash/main.go#L197).

## User-set constraints

Any option in the menu must respect:

1. **One result per line (greppable).** Each record renders on its own
   line. Rules out tree-form / path-prefix-grouped output.
2. **`tokens_in` honesty.** If we add aliases / positionals / interning,
   the daemon must tokenize what the agent literally typed, not the
   post-expansion canonical form.
3. **Headers stay by default.** The `§<verb>: ...` context
   header is on by default; compact mode is opt-in.
4. **Wire parity.** Anything dropped from pretty must still ride the
   wire (JSON / msgpack). Only the agent-facing rendering changes.

## Phase 1 — Measure

Goal: turn "where do our tokens go?" from intuition into data.

1. **Mine the existing ledger.** Use `ash report` and `ash metrics` against
   `.ash/ledger.db` to surface, per verb:
   - total `tokens_out`, p50 / p95 `tokens_out`
   - call count and total `tokens_out × calls` (where to optimize wins)
   - `tokens_out / bytes_out` ratio (which verbs tokenize wastefully)
   - `tokens_in` distribution, especially for `read` / `write` / `edit` /
     `diff` (where stdin payloads dominate)
2. **Augment `ash bench`.** The bench harness already compares ash vs.
   bash; extend its case corpus to cover every live verb, including
   pretty-form-only variants (e.g. `find` with and without `--with_meta`,
   `grep` with and without `--files_only`, `git diff --stat true|false`).
   See [docs/bench.md](docs/bench.md) and
   [internal/verbs/bench/](internal/verbs/bench/).
3. **Decompose hot verbs.** For the top 2-3 verbs by total token output,
   mechanically partition `tokens_out` into:
   - header (the `§<verb>: ...` line + truncation hint)
   - per-record overhead (e.g. the date column in `find --with_meta`,
     the `(N matches)` parenthetical in `grep`)
   - record body
   Goal: a one-page table of "where the tokens go" that drives Phase 2.
4. **Write findings into a session note** at
   `docs/session-notes/YYYY-MM-DD-encoding-measurement.md`.

The output of Phase 1 is **the table**: per-verb tokens × frequency,
with the body-vs-overhead breakdown for hot verbs. Without it, picking
options is a guess.

## Phase 2 — Options menu (data-informed selection)

The full menu, marked by whether the constraints rule it in or out.
Rank within tiers is the recommended starting order, but the table from
Phase 1 may reorder.

### Output-side options

| # | Option | Survives constraints? | Tier | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | `--fields a,b,c` projection per verb | Yes | A | Each record still per-line. Generalizes `--with_meta` / `--stat` / `--files_only`. Needs schema discipline (already partly in `help` registry). |
| O2 | `--compact true` global (drops header + truncation hint) | Yes (opt-in only) | B | Per-call constant savings (~10-30 tokens). Headers stay on by default per constraint #3. |
| O3 | Path-prefix compression (group by parent, indent) | **No** | — | Ruled out by constraint #1. |
| O4 | Sharpen grep lean form (drop `(N matches)` parenthetical) | Yes (opt-in only) | B | Small per-file savings. Sharpens existing pattern. |
| O5 | Per-record column elision (drop date in `find --with_meta`, drop encoding+mtime in `read` header) | Yes | A | Mechanical, easy to A/B in bench. ~5 tokens/record on `find`; significant at scale. |
| O6 | New `--format` values: `tsv`, `lean`, `fields:<csv>` | Yes | C | Requires extending per-verb PrettyResponse signature (or threading format through `req.Args`). Subsumes O1+O2. |
| O7 | Tokenizer-aware micro-opts (favor sequences that merge to single cl100k tokens, ASCII separators) | Yes | C | Real but small (1-5%). Only worth it if Phase 1 highlights a hot encoding choice. |
| O8 | `--max_tokens N` budget knob | Yes | C | Speculative until ledger shows actual overruns. |

### Input-side options

All input-side options share a **prerequisite**: change the daemon's
`tokens_in` computation to count the *original argv* (transmitted from
client to daemon as a separate field on `proto.Request`), not the
reconstructed `PrettyRequest` from the parsed map. Without this,
constraint #2 is violated and we're fudging the meter.

| # | Option | Survives constraints? | Tier | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| I0 | **Argv-honesty rework**: ship original argv on `proto.Request`, tokenize that | Yes | A (prerequisite for I1-I4) | Adds an `Argv []string` field to `proto.Request`; daemon switches `tokens_in` source. Backwards-compatible if absent. |
| I1 | Positional dominant arg (`ash find <path>`, `ash read <path>`, `ash grep <pattern> <path>`) | Yes | A | Saves `--path ` / `--pattern ` boilerplate every call. Requires per-verb dominant-arg policy and lifting the positional rejection at `cmd/ash/main.go:197`. |
| I2 | Argv path interning (`@root`, `@cwd`) | Yes | B | Big savings on absolute-path-heavy invocations (project root is ~10-20 tokens repeated everywhere). Resolver runs in client; tokenization counts literal `@root`. |
| I3 | Short flag aliases (`-p`, `-g`, `-c`) | Yes | C | 1 token per flag. Conflict risk (`-p` for path vs pattern in grep). |
| I4 | Short verb aliases (`f`/`g`/`r`/`e`/`w`/`d`) | Yes | D | 1-2 tokens per call. Pollutes surface; defer until I1 lands and we measure residual `tokens_in`. |
| I5 | Stop sorting keys in PrettyRequest | **No** | — | Negligible savings, real determinism loss. Skip. |
| I6 | Drop `ash` prefix in PrettyRequest | **No** | — | The agent literally types it. Removing under-reports cost. Skip. |

### Cross-cutting

| # | Option | Survives constraints? | Tier | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Encoding registry (`--encoding` global → format-aware PrettyResponse) | Yes | C | Architectural home for O1+O2+O4+O6. Ship after Phase 1 data + at least one Tier A win has validated the pattern. |
| X2 | Flip defaults to compact | **No** | — | Ruled out by constraint #3 (headers stay by default). Could revisit if Phase 1 shows headers are dead weight, but not by default. |

## Phase 3 — Pick & implement

After Phase 1 produces the data, the recommended selection is:

- **Always do I0** (argv-honesty rework) before any input-side option, so
  the meter is honest.
- **One Tier A output option**: pick the one Phase 1 shows the largest
  `tokens × calls` win for. Likely O5 (column elision in `find --with_meta`
  and `read` header) or O1 (`--fields` projection) — but data decides.
- **One Tier A input option**: I1 (positional dominant arg) is the
  universal win and only changes one file.

Each option ships behind a flag, with `ash bench` A/B verifying the
expected savings. Update `docs/bench.md` with the per-option case.

If the savings are real and the surface holds up, then evaluate X1
(encoding registry) as the unifying refactor — but only after at least
one Tier A option has validated the design space.

## Verification

- Re-run `ash bench` with the new cases; confirm per-case `tokens_out`
  delta matches the prediction. Reject any option whose measured savings
  are below ~5% of the verb's typical `tokens_out`.
- Inspect ledger after a full session of recursive use: `ash report
  --since 1h --verb <verb>` should show p50 / p95 `tokens_out` dropping
  on the affected verbs and **no regressions** on others.
- Write a session note (`docs/session-notes/YYYY-MM-DD-encoding-results.md`)
  capturing measured deltas and any agent-ergonomics friction.

## Critical files

- [internal/proto/pretty.go](internal/proto/pretty.go) — `PrettyRequest`
  (token-input source).
- [cmd/ashd/main.go:140-142](cmd/ashd/main.go#L140-L142) — where the
  daemon tokenizes; the I0 change lands here.
- [cmd/ash/main.go:172-217](cmd/ash/main.go#L172-L217) — `extractFormat`
  and `parseFlags`; positional / alias / interning changes land here.
- [internal/proto/proto.go](internal/proto/proto.go) — `Request` struct;
  the I0 change adds `Argv` here.
- [internal/verbs/verbs.go:46-61](internal/verbs/verbs.go#L46-L61) —
  PrettyResponse registry; any per-verb output change touches the
  corresponding `internal/verbs/<verb>/` package.
- [internal/verbs/find/find.go](internal/verbs/find/find.go),
  [internal/verbs/grep/grep.go](internal/verbs/grep/grep.go),
  [internal/verbs/read/read.go](internal/verbs/read/read.go) — the
  three highest-traffic pretty renderers; likely O5 / O1 candidates.
- [internal/verbs/bench/](internal/verbs/bench/) — extend the case
  corpus here for Phase 1 measurement and Phase 3 verification.
- [docs/bench.md](docs/bench.md) — bench harness docs; update with new
  cases.

## Out of scope

- Changing the wire format (msgpack stays).
- Compression of output (gzip / base64 — base64 tokenizes worse).
- Changing the tokenizer (cl100k_base is the right choice for the
  agents we serve).
- Anything that violates the four user-set constraints.
